questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Lanky
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 (Plump)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Lanky"** refers to someone who is tall, thin, and often awkward in movement or appearance. (दुबला-पतला और लंबा)

 
 
• **Example:** The lanky boy struggled to fit into the small chair during the meeting.
 
 
 
• **"Plump"** is the antonym of "Lanky" and refers to someone or something that is slightly fat or rounded in shape, indicating a fuller appearance. (गोलमटोल)
 
 
• **Example:** The plump cat lay lazily on the couch, basking in the sunlight.
 
 
 
• Hence, the opposite of **"Lanky"** is **"Plump"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 (Plump)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Rare** (दुर्लभ): Something uncommon, unusual, or unique.

 
 
• **Example:** It is rare to find such a talented artist in this small town.
 
 
 
• **Rectangular** (आयताकार): Having the shape of a rectangle, with four right angles.
 
 
• **Example:** The rectangular table was perfect for the dining room.
 
 
 
• **Congenital** (जन्मजात): Referring to a condition or trait that is present from birth.
 
 
• **Example:** The child was diagnosed with a congenital heart defect.

He doesn’t travel such more/ these days/ because he is not well.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. He doesn’t travel such more .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence contains an error in part 2: "**He doesn’t travel such more**."
 
• The phrase "**such more**" is incorrect. The correct expression should be "**so much**" to indicate a reduced frequency of travel.
 
• The word "**such**" is generally used before nouns or noun phrases, while "**so**" is used before adjectives or adverbs.

Correct sentence: *He doesn’t travel **so much** these days because he is not well*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The usage of "**such**" and "**so**" often causes confusion:
 
 
• **Such:** Used with nouns to emphasize their quality or extent.
 
 
• Example: She is *such a good teacher*.
 
 
 
• **So:** Used with adjectives or adverbs to emphasize the degree.
 
 
• Example: He runs *so fast*.
 
 
 
 
 
• In this context, "**so much**" is the correct usage to describe the extent of traveling.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Most of the passengers complained/ that the speed of the bus/ was usual fast.

options.text: that the speed of the bus

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. was usual fast.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the phrase **"was usual fast."**
 
• The word **"usual"** is an adjective and cannot modify the adverb **"fast."** Instead, the correct form should be the adverb **"usually."**
 
• The correct sentence should read: **"Most of the passengers complained that the speed of the bus was usually fast."**

Correct sentence: *Most of the passengers complained that the speed of the bus was usually fast.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adjectives vs. Adverbs:**
 
 
• **Adjectives:** Describe nouns or pronouns (e.g., "usual speed").
 
• **Adverbs:** Modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs (e.g., "usually fast").
 
 
 
• It is important to choose the correct form based on the function of the word in the sentence to ensure grammatical accuracy.
